title: A normalized cone on the identity characterizes a final object
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and weak contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For simplicial sets $X,Y$, define their join by $(X\star Y)_r=X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{u+v+1=r}X_u\times Y_v$, with simplicial operators induced by restricting the ordered concatenation of the $X$-vertices followed by the $Y$-vertices. Write $X^{\triangleright}=X\star\Delta^0$, with $X$ as its base and the additional vertex as its cone point. Let $J$ be a quasicategory and $t\in J_0$. Then $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ is weakly contractible for every $j\in J_0$ if and only if there exists a simplicial map $F:J^{\triangleright}\to J$ whose restriction to the base $J$ is $\operatorname{id}_J$, which sends the cone point to $t$, and whose restriction to the edge $\{t\}^{\triangleright}\cong\Delta^1$ is the constant simplicial map at $t$ (the degenerate edge $\operatorname{id}_t$).

source.place: Kerodon Corollary 4.7.3.21 (02J4), assertion (1), expressed through the defining join universal property of the slice: a section J to J over t is a map from the right cone restricting to the identity; the prescribed value at t is the degenerate edge. For the right-pinched mapping-space convention see Construction 4.6.5.1 and Propositions 4.6.5.5 and 4.6.5.10. These are Kerodon references, not Stacks tags. Online text read; archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Put $E=J_{/t}$ and let $q:E\to J$ be restriction to the base in the join-slice construction of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. The hypotheses are exactly that $J$ is a quasicategory and $t$ a vertex. That node supplies a quasicategory $E$, a right fibration $q$, and identifies its fiber $E_j$ with the right-pinched $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ as a Kan complex. In coordinates this fiber consists of $\Delta^{n+1}=\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to J$ constant at $j$ on the whole initial face and with last vertex $t$, exactly the mapping-space convention in the item. The vertex $e\in E_0$ given by the degenerate edge $\operatorname{id}_t$ lies over $t$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: the slice projection; Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX) for its fibers.

proof.text: Assume every $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ is weakly contractible. The fiber identifications of Step 1 show that every vertex fiber of $q$ is a weakly contractible Kan complex. Its right-fibration property therefore satisfies all hypotheses of [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers], which makes $q$ a trivial Kan fibration, including surjectivity on vertices. No global weak equivalence of $q$ or Kan property of $J$ has been assumed.

source.place: Proof, forward implication; expands Corollary 4.7.3.12 via the general criterion of 01NU.

proof.text: The inclusion $i:\{t\}\hookrightarrow J$ is injective in every degree: the constant simplex at $t$ is a singleton subset in each degree. Let $a:\{t\}\to E$ be constant at the vertex $e=\operatorname{id}_t$, and let the bottom map be $\operatorname{id}_J:J\to J$. Since $q(e)=t$, the square $qa=\operatorname{id}_J\,i$ commutes strictly. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to this square and Step 2. It supplies a simplicial section $G:J\to E$ with $qG=\operatorname{id}_J$ and $G(t)=e$, both as literal simplicial equalities, not merely up to homotopy.

source.place: Proof, forward implication: extend the prescribed identity vertex to a section; Stacks Tag 08NM is the existing generic lifting tool.

proof.text: Unwind the join slice of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. For a simplex $\sigma\in J_u$, write $g_\sigma=G(\sigma):\Delta^{u+1}\to J$. Its initial face is $\sigma$, its last vertex is $t$, and $g_{\sigma\beta}=g_\sigma\circ\Delta(\beta\star\operatorname{id}_{[0]})$ for every monotone $\beta:[k]\to[u]$, since $G$ is simplicial. Define $F$ to be the identity on the base and constant at $t$ on the cone-point simplices. On a mixed $r$-simplex $(\sigma,*)$, with $\sigma\in J_u$, $v\geq0$, and $r=u+v+1$, define $F_r(\sigma,*)=g_\sigma\circ\Delta(\rho_{u,v})$, where $\rho_{u,v}:[r]\to[u+1]$ fixes $0,\ldots,u$ and sends every remaining index to $u+1$. To check an operator $\alpha:[m]\to[r]$, if its image meets both blocks, its initial block has $k+1$ indices and determines $\beta:[k]\to[u]$; then $\rho_{u,v}\alpha=(\beta\star\operatorname{id}_{[0]})\rho_{k,m-k-1}$, and the displayed simplicial identity for $g$ gives compatibility. If its image lies entirely in the initial block, compatibility is the base equation $g_\sigma|_{\Delta^u}=\sigma$; if entirely in the final block, it is the last-vertex equation $g_\sigma(u+1)=t$. These cases cover every face and degeneracy, so $F$ is simplicial. Its edge at $t$ is $g_t=G(t)=e$, the degenerate edge. Conversely, a normalized $F$ defines $G(\sigma)=F\circ(\sigma\star\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0})$; precomposition with $\beta\star\operatorname{id}$ proves simpliciality, and the base and edge conditions give $qG=\operatorname{id}_J$ and $G(t)=e$. Restriction to base, cone-point, and mixed simplices with the maps $\rho_{u,v}$ shows that these constructions are inverse.

source.place: Join/slice defining universal property; this is the explicit translation of the section in (1), also used in 02J5.

proof.text: Now assume the normalized $F$ exists, and take its section $G$ from Step 4. The degenerate edge $\operatorname{id}_t$ is an equivalence (it is its own inverse, with degenerate triangle witnesses), so [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final] makes $e$ a final object of $E$. In particular $B_j=\operatorname{Map}_E(G(j),e)$ is a weakly contractible Kan complex for every $j$. Postcomposition of right-pinched mapping simplices with the simplicial maps $G$ and $q$ gives maps $s_j:A_j=\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)\to B_j$ and $r_j:B_j\to A_j$. Their endpoint conditions use $G(t)=e$, $qG(j)=j$, and $q(e)=t$. On every $n$-simplex the composite $r_js_j$ is postcomposition with $qG=\operatorname{id}_J$, so it is the identity map of simplicial sets. Thus $A_j$ is a retract of $B_j$.

source.place: Proof, reverse implication: the displayed two mapping-space maps and finality of the slice identity, using 02J2.

proof.text: For completeness the retract in Step 5 preserves the weak-contractibility meaning fixed in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Since $B_j$ is nonempty, $r_j$ makes $A_j$ nonempty; its component set is a retract of the singleton component set of $B_j$, hence a singleton. At any base point $a$ of $|A_j|$, the maps on homotopy groups induced by $s_j$ and $r_j$, based at $|s_j|(a)$ on $|B_j|$, compose to the identity. Each $\pi_n(|A_j|,a)$ for $n\geq1$ is consequently a retract of the trivial group $\pi_n(|B_j|,|s_j|(a))$, hence is trivial. Therefore $A_j\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This holds for every $j$, proving the reverse implication and the stated equivalence.

source.place: Proof, last two sentences: write out the elementary retract-of-a-contractible-space argument on components and based homotopy groups.

lean.statement: theorem normalized_final_cone {J : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory J] (t : J _⦋0⦌) : (∀ j : J _⦋0⦌, IsContractible (mappingSpace J j t)) ↔ ∃ F : ∀ n : SimplexCategory, J.obj (op n) → J _⦋n.len + 1⦌, (∀ (n : SimplexCategory) (s : J.obj (op n)), J.map (SimplexCategory.δ (Fin.last (n.len + 1))).op (F n s) = s) ∧ (∀ (n : SimplexCategory) (s : J.obj (op n)), J.map (SimplexCategory.const ⦋0⦌ ⦋n.len + 1⦌ (Fin.last (n.len + 1))).op (F n s) = t) ∧ (∀ (m n : SimplexCategory) (a : m ⟶ n) (s : J.obj (op n)), F m (J.map a.op s) = J.map (appendLast a).op (F n s)) ∧ F ⦋0⦌ t = J.σ 0 t
lean.note: The right-cone map is written in its full compatible-simplex coordinates: base and apex restrictions, every appendLast operator, and the strict degenerate t-edge. The docstring gives the inverse mixed-simplex formula. No second join definition is introduced.
